_README: TEMPLATE ONLY — every value below is invented. The hosts are .invalid and
will never resolve, and the coordinates are round placeholders, not a
surveyed site. Deploying this file as-is polls nothing.
A real deployment supplies its own node list through the runtime copy in
backend/data/runtime/ (seeded from here on first boot, and the winner once
it exists) or by pointing BLAH2_NODES_FILE somewhere else. Receiver
positions are private: the API publishes every node displaced by
services/public_location.py, so the true ones must not re-enter this repo,
Live blah2 retnodes polled over HTTP by services/blah2_bridge.py.
One entry per node; the bridge runs one polling task per entry, so adding a
node here is the only change needed to ingest it.
Required: node_id, detection_url, rx_lat, rx_lon, tx_lat, tx_lon, fc_hz.
Optional (defaults in blah2_bridge.py): rx_alt_ft, tx_alt_ft, fs_hz,
doppler_min, doppler_max, min_doppler, beam_width_deg, max_range_km, notes.
Geometry must match the real hardware — tx/rx positions and fc feed the
bistatic solver directly, so an error here misplaces every target from that
node. Verify with GET /api/test/node/<node_ref>/verification after a change;
the ref is the node's key in GET /api/radar/nodes.

nodes.notes: Placeholder. Two receivers at one site, each on its own illuminator: reusing one node's TX or fc for the other misplaces every target from it.
